clue.text: The eccentric gave a car next such prodigality!

indicators.note: something eccentric is odd and off-centre, so the following words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a showy person who has handed over a car as well as everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The eccentric' looks like a person; 'eccentric' is the anagram signal on GAVE A CAR NEXT, twelve letters that rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigality is wasteful, lavish spending, the same idea as reckless excess.

clue.text: Quick to get out of jam

explanation.surface: Advice to escape a tight spot fast.
explanation.definitionFit: An express train is fast; to express juice is to squeeze or press it out.

clue.text: A supporter of the pig and pony

explanation.surface: Someone backs both the pig and the pony, as at a country fair.
explanation.walkthrough: A pig's trotter is its foot, which literally supports it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's foot holds it up; a horse bred or trained for trotting races is the second sense.

clue.text: Take turns later maybe neat solution

indicators.note: a solution is something dissolved and remixed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion that turn-taking later might tidily solve a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' looks like the answer to a problem; it signals mixing up LATER NEAT, and 'maybe' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something by turns, one after the other, is to swap back and forth.

clue.text: Making a return once more

explanation.surface: Someone coming back for another go.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage it means back, in return; it also means another time, a second time.

clue.text: Crowded dwelling for six-footers

parts.note: six-footers suggests very tall people, but means insects, which have six feet

explanation.surface: A cramped house for tall people.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects that live in huge colonies build mounds of earth as their nests.

clue.text: Duck boxed in picture

indicators.note: the duck letter is placed in the box word

parts.note: boxed suggests a carton, the cardboard box something is packed in
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A duck is packed into a frame or shown in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a nought in cricket, the letter O; it goes in CARTON. 'Duck' looks like the bird or a verb; Donald Duck adds to the false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous drawing or animated film is a kind of illustration.

clue.text: Bookings made with certain misgivings

explanation.surface: Someone books seats while having doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: Seats or rooms held in advance are one sense; doubts or qualms are the other.

clue.text: Get some benefit from a noble deed

explanation.surface: Someone profits from an act of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: To make use of something for gain is one sense; a heroic feat is the other, as in tales of knightly deeds.

clue.text: Workers absorbing article about a star

indicators.note: the workers take in, or soak up, the other pieces, so those go inside

parts.note: ants are the stock crossword workers, from the worker caste of the colony
a is the indefinite article
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Labourers soak up a newspaper piece about a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is the bright red star in the constellation Scorpius.

clue.text: He gives a moving performance in 25

definitions.text: He gives a moving performance in 25

parts.words: He gives a moving performance in 25
parts.note: a moving performance sounds like a touching piece of acting, but means someone who physically moves scenery on stage at a playhouse

explanation.surface: An actor who brings audiences to tears at the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is the answer to 25 across, the playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagehand moves sets and backdrops between scenes during a play.

clue.text: Choosy individual with a marked preference

definitions.text: Choosy individual with a marked preference

parts.words: Choosy individual with a marked preference
parts.note: reads as a fussy person, but means someone who chooses and marks a ballot paper with a cross

explanation.surface: A fussy person with strong likes and dislikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter chooses a candidate by putting a mark on the ballot paper, which is literally a marked preference.

clue.text: One is made to accept an order that's offensive

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in, or accept, another piece placed inside them
the words one is are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A person is forced to obey a command they find objectionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One is made' reads as a person being forced; 'made' is the anagram signal, and OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour, which 'to accept' places inside the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noisome is unpleasant or disgusting, often of a smell, so it is objectionable.

clue.text: The fighting man's face-saving device

parts.note: face-saving suggests a way of avoiding embarrassment, but here it is a guard that literally protects a soldier's face

explanation.surface: A soldier's trick for avoiding humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: The movable front of a helmet protected an armoured knight's face in battle.

clue.text: Transport for those wanting personal attention

definitions.text: Transport for those wanting personal attention

parts.words: Transport for those wanting personal attention
parts.note: personal attention sounds like pampering, but means people needing medical care to their own bodies

explanation.surface: A chauffeur service for customers who want to be fussed over.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency vehicle carries the sick and injured to hospital for treatment.

clue.text: Where horses are given a drink in town

definitions.text: Where horses are given a drink in town

parts.note: bays are reddish-brown horses
water is something to drink, as when horses are watered

explanation.surface: A place in a town where horses are watered.
explanation.walkthrough: BAYSWATER is a district of west London, next to Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: The district is a part of London, the capital, so a place in town.

clue.text: Aim to include every form of hesitation and disloyalty

indicators.note: the first piece takes in the following pieces, which go inside it

parts.note: to aim at doing something is to try it
each and every are near synonyms
er is the sound of someone hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to cover every kind of dithering and betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aim' looks like a noun meaning goal; it is the verb, to attempt, and the 'form of hesitation' is the sound a speaker makes while pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal of trust or faith is what both words describe.

clue.text: Cheer for most of the players at end of game

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses some of its final letters

parts.note: a football or cricket team has eleven players

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Applause for nearly all the team when a match finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops EN from ELEVEN, leaving ELEV; then AT and E, the last letter of 'game'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift someone's spirits is to raise them up, to buoy them.

clue.text: Coy pals' drunken song

indicators.note: the letters stagger about like a drunk, out of order

explanation.surface: Shy friends sing a tipsy tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean style of ballad, originally from Trinidad.

clue.text: It's light to carry

parts.note: reads as something not heavy to carry, but means a lamp you hold in your hand

explanation.surface: A remark that an object weighs little.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-held lamp or flaming brand is a source of illumination that you carry about.

clue.text: The sunburned man's touching line

parts.note: someone sunburned or bronzed has a tan
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A suntanned man's emotional remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' looks like moving or emotional; it means meeting a curve at one point.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry it is a straight line meeting a curve at a single point without crossing it.

clue.text: A roll containing nothing but chicken

indicators.note: the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, a roster
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A bread roll with nothing but chicken in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' looks like bread; it is a list. 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock is a male domestic fowl.

clue.text: Applied decoration to finished poem

parts.note: over means ended or finished, as in the game is over
a lay is a narrative poem or ballad

explanation.surface: Someone adds ornament to a completed verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlay is a decorative layer laid on top of a surface, such as gold leaf on wood.

clue.text: Speak up about sailors' stories

explanation.surface: Someone talks about tales told by seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: To yarn is to chat or talk at length; old sailors were known for spinning tall tales.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to talk or chat at length; as a noun, tall tales told by seamen.

clue.text: Left with original backing — swell!

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for original is read backwards

parts.note: something original is new and not copied
a swell and a toff are both old slang for a fashionable, upper-class gentleman

explanation.surface: Someone departs with their first supporters, which they find marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NEW into WEN. 'swell!' looks like an exclamation of delight; it is the noun, a toff.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed or exploded both fit: to go away from a place is to have departed it.

clue.text: No conscientious guy needs to hurry

explanation.surface: A careless worker has to rush.
explanation.walkthrough: To scamp work is to do it carelessly and skimpily, so one who does so is no conscientious worker.
explanation.definitionFit: One who skimps on a job is a careless worker; to dash or scurry off briskly is the other sense.

clue.text: Some people seethe at repellent plays

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, a run lying inside them

explanation.surface: Certain people fume at disgusting dramas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals a run inside 'seethe at repellent'; 'people' is part of the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama as a whole, the staging of stage works, is called the stage or drama.

clue.text: Seeing Roman rotters misbehaving, he made complaint

indicators.note: the letters of the words behave badly and fall out of order

explanation.surface: On seeing some badly behaved Romans, a man protested.
explanation.definitionFit: One who protests or objects forcefully is a protester, a person who complains.
